question.text: This northern neighbor of Germany lies on the Jutland peninsula. It also controls Greenland.
question.clue: During its occupation by the Nazis, this country's resistance movement saved nearly all of its Jews, and its king apocryphally wore a yellow star in solidarity.

swap.leadin: The continent of Europe is home to many notable seas of the world.
swap.text: This sea in eastern Europe names the region containing Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia. Stockholm, Sweden, lies on the shores of this sea.
swap.clue: The defeat of Wendish tribes along this body's southern shores led to the rise of the Viking Age, and the modern Kaliningrad Oblast borders this body.

question.leadin: Leather cannons used by this man's army allowed his artillery unprecedented mobility in combat.
question.text: Name this Swedish ruler nicknamed "The Lion of the North," who was advised by Axel Oxenstierna and transformed Sweden into a leading European power.
question.clue: This ruler's chancellor, Axel Oxenstierna, continued to fight the war in which this ruler died while fighting Wallenstein at the Battle of Lutzen.

swap.text: This Norwegian terrorist set off a car bomb in Oslo and carried out a mass shooting in Utoya, which he claimed to do in order to fight against the forces of Islam and multiculturalism.
swap.clue: First, name this right-wing extremist who was also responsible for the Utoya massacre, in which he opened fire on a crowd, killing 69 and injuring 66 at an AUF summer camp.

question.leadin: This country formed a dual monarchy with Denmark after the collapse of the Kalmar Union in 1521.
question.text: Name this country whose kings include Harald Hardrada.
question.clue: After referenda in 1974 and 1992, this country, like Switzerland, declined to join the E.U.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about polar expeditions that used the ship Fram.
swap.text: This Norwegian explorer sailed the Fram to Antarctica in a 1911 expedition that was the first to reach the South Pole, beating Robert Falcon Scott's by one month. This explorer and Scott now co-name an American research station at the South Pole.
swap.answerHtml: Roald Amundsen (“ROH-all AW-moon-sen”) [or Roald Engelbregt Gravning Amundsen; accept Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station]
swap.clue: The goal of Scott's expedition was to be the first men to reach the South Pole. When they arrived, however, they were devastated to learn that a crew led by this Norwegian had beaten them to it by four weeks.

question.leadin: This nation was forced to cede Petsamo in the Moscow Peace Treaty.
question.text: Name this north European nation, which fought alongside Nazi Germany during the siege of Leningrad. It lost the Continuation War to the Soviet Union, to which it leased Porkkala, roughly twenty miles from Helsinki.
question.answerHtml: Republic of Finland [or Suomi; or Suomen Tasavalta; or Republiken Finland]
question.clue: Due to the nationalistic drivings of Johan Snellman, this country underwent a namesake language strife in the 1800s. This country won the Battle of Raate Road.

swap.leadin: This god transformed into a snake to retrieve the divine mead of inspiration.
swap.text: Name this chief god of the Norse myth system. He has one eye and is advised by the ravens Hunin and Mugin.

question.leadin: These people use a unit of measurement called a poronkusema, which is based on how far a reindeer can move before urinating.
question.text: Name these people of northern Scandinavia and Russia whose economy traditionally depended on reindeer herding.
question.answerHtml: Sámi [or Saami; or Sabme; accept Lapplanders but politely inform the person giving the answer that this term is not preferred anymore]
question.clue: Protests against the construction of the Alta hydroelectric power station strengthened activism for these people's rights and led to the 1989 formation of their first parliament.

swap.leadin: It arose over the control of the Hanko naval base and was prosecuted by the coalition government of Risto Ryti.
swap.text: Name this war which saw the use of the Mannerheim line in an attempt to repel a Soviet invasion.
swap.clue: During this war, fighting at Raate Road ended the battle of Suomussalmi.

question.text: Zealand and Amager islands make up this city, home to Tivoli Gardens and a statue of a mermaid.
question.clue: In later years, the Swedes, British, and Germans all attacked the city, but none of these attacks yielded any permanent change.

swap.text: Meatballs allegedly first arrived in Sweden after this monarch fled to the Ottoman Empire after losing the Battle of Poltava ("poll-TAH-vuh"). This monarch led Sweden during the Great Northern War.
swap.answerHtml: Charles XII [or Carl XII; or Carolus Rex; prompt on Charles or Carl or Carolus]
swap.clue: He was killed while besieging the fortress of Fredriksten, after which his army was decimated by a brutal winter while making this ruler's namesake "Death March."

question.leadin: Cardinal Mazarin remarked that if all the ministers of Europe were on the same boat, this person would be at the helm.
question.text: Name this Swedish politician. He served as regent for Gustavus Adolphus in his absence and, after his death in battle, regent for his young daughter Christina.

swap.text: Due to skepticism over Henson's voyage, the first undisputed expedition to the North Pole was led by this Norwegian explorer, the first to reach the South Pole and traverse the Northwest Passage.
swap.clue: This person led the crew that disappeared searching for the airship Italia and was the first to successfully navigate the North-west Passage in a boat, the Gjoa .

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the ways in which Vikings governed their territory after settling down from raiding.
question.text: This Icelandic deliberative body, the world's oldest still-extant parliament, was established by Norse settlers in the 900s CE to resolve disputes.
question.clue: It was disbanded in favor of the High Court from 1800 to 1845, when Christian VIII allowed it to reconvene.

swap.text: This Norwegian explorer worked for the League as a High Commissioner for Refugees, winning the Nobel Prize for his efforts in 1922. He introduced a namesake passport for stateless persons.
swap.clue: He prodded the British navy and directed the Red Cross in overseeing the repatriation of over 400,000 Soviet prisoners of war, which earned him the Nobel Peace Prize.

question.text: For Frederick I's rule and some years afterwards the riksdag was dominated by these two political parties, one of which assumed control of parliament in 1738 before giving way to the other in 1765.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Norway's civil war era.
swap.text: The civil war developed into a war between the aristocratic Bagler faction and a rebellious commoner faction named for this material. The faction got its name because its members were supposedly so poor that they made their shoes from this material.
swap.answerHtml: birchbark [accept Birkebeiner, Birkebeinar, Birkebein Party, or Birkebein faction; prompt on wood or bark]

question.text: Following the Battle of Poltava, Lewanhaupt and Charles adandoned everything leading to this time period of Norwegian history in which the Russians decimated the population of Norway.
question.answerHtml: The Greater Wrath [accept: isoviha from Will Alston; accept The Great Discord]

swap.leadin: Name these people who helped convert Scandinavia to Christianity.
swap.text: The English bishop Grimketel speedily canonized this Norwegian king, who was killed at Stiklestad by rebellious farmers.
swap.answerHtml: St. Olaf [or Olaf II; or Olaf Haraldsson; prompt on “Olaf”; do not accept or prompt on “Olaf Trvggyvason”]
